metadata.title: Prequential Streaming Evaluation of Stateful Time-Series Forecasters with Online Conformal Calibration: A Diagnostic Atlas and the preqts Harness
metadata.description:
Forecasting may be deployed as a stream: observations arrive one by one, the model updates, and its prediction intervals are expected to remain useful as the series changes. We provide a prequential streaming evaluation harness, released as the open-source package preqts: it implements Dawid's predict-then-observe-then-update protocol behind a StatefulForecaster interface with an explicit covariate-arrival policy, and records four trajectories per method: rolling scaled error, rolling empirical coverage, rolling weighted quantile loss, and cumulative measured compute time. The package supports stateful and replay-based forecasters; the experiment reported here uses replay-based Theta wrappers and does not compare constant-cost native state updates. The harness is embedded in an atlas that characterizes each series with ten diagnostic families (stationarity, autocorrelation, seasonality, filters, change points, volatility, distribution and complexity, fractal structure, nonlinear dynamics, and cross-series causality) and then forecasts it with a method catalogue spanning classical, statistical, gradient-boosted, deep, and foundation-model methods. Using the harness we test a concrete claim: that online conformal calibration keeps streaming intervals at nominal under distribution shift. On fifteen series that span distinct regimes and include white-noise and random-walk negative controls, wrapping a Theta point forecaster in Adaptive Conformal Inference or Conformal-PID control reduces the mean absolute coverage error at the nominal 80% level from 0.0416 (raw Theta) and 0.0599 (seasonal-naive) to 0.0057 and 0.0060, a seven-to-tenfold reduction, and shrinks the across-case span of the final coverage from 0.19-0.40 to 0.04, without changing the point forecast. Calibrated coverage is also near target on the two generated negative controls, which provide limited checks against simple predictable-versus-unpredictable confounds but cannot rule out all leakage. The contribution is the reusable prequential harness and an artifact-backed comparison under the protocol defined below.

Source code, admitted inputs and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_ChronoScope . Research atlas: https://chronoscope.fasl-work.com . Not peer reviewed.
metadata.version_notes: Clarifies the historical smoothing-plus-drift adapter, replay costs and finite-case evidence boundaries; original streaming measurements are retained.
